title: Facade Code Framework daemon API
description: A single JSON-RPC 2.0 frame. Success result and change types are selected by the corresponding request or watch.

AgentCreator.description: The source of an agent's start, as displayed to the caller.

AgentRemoval.description: The recorded cause of an agent record's removal.

oneOf.description: The CLI has not shown what it is doing yet, within 30 seconds of its start or resume.
The CLI is working, or stopped working less than a second ago.

The CLI waits for the person; `state_detail.kind` says for what. A menu or question it draws
in place of its input counts, with `kind` `unknown` where it did not say, also while it
starts.

A turn ended while no terminal showed the agent. It stays so until one does. Work before the
CLI is asked to do anything is no turn: an Enter typed into it asks, unless it answers a
question the CLI shows. Words after the CLI's name at its start are the CLI's own and ask
nothing.
The CLI is not working and waits for nothing.

The CLI reported an error or its screen shows that the turn it reported ended failed, or,
started by its rule's name, it showed nothing of what it is doing within 30 seconds of its
start or resume.
The CLI's process ended; `state_detail.how` says how, where that is known.
Nothing shows what the CLI is doing; `state_detail.reason` says why.
A Guest is connected and can take messages.

cli.description:
The name a start gives: a built-in's, such as `claude`, or the name of a CLI the settings
file adds.

display_name.description: The name people know it by: a built-in's, such as `Claude Code`, or an added CLI's own.

available.description: Whether it can be started: its entry is right and its program is found.

problem.description:
Why it cannot be started: what is wrong with its entry, or that its program cannot run where
it would start, each said by its setting. Omitted where it can.

not_installed.description:
A built-in CLI whose entry has no problem and names no program of its own, and whose
program is not found where the start would run: not installed. Only with `available` false.
A client may leave it out of its list instead of showing it as one that cannot start.
Omitted otherwise.

overrides.description: Whether a start can choose its model and its effort (CLIS-1.4).

CliInfo.description: A CLI a start can run: an entry of Facade Code Framework's settings file (CONFIGURATION-2.1).

oneOf.description: Typed into the recipient's terminal and submitted.
Returned by a snapshot of the recipient's `messages` topic.
A message to the person: delivered to one or more member windows' subscriptions.
Returned to the sending command as its reply.

status.description: `pending` while the message is being delivered, then `success` or `failure`.

reason.description: Why it was not delivered. Omitted unless it failed.

text_written.description: How much of the message reached the recipient's terminal.

enter_written.description:
Whether the message's submission key (Enter or Tab) reached the recipient's terminal.
Omitted when the write outcome is unknown, for example when the key was still queued at the
deadline or a restart interrupted delivery.

deadline.description:
When a pending delivery fails if the message is not delivered by then. Omitted once it is
settled.

delivered_via.description: How the message was delivered. Omitted unless it was.

delivered_at.description: When the message was delivered. Omitted unless it was.

oneOf.description: The recipient ended, or its terminal stopped taking input, before the message was delivered.

A draft held the recipient's input until the deadline. A draft that is not the message's own
is never typed over.
A menu, login, or question of the recipient's CLI held its input until the deadline.

The recipient's input was not recognized as empty until the deadline: its screen did not
show it as its CLI's rule describes it.

The input was empty. The delivery deadline passed before the paste and submission key
could both reach the terminal and be confirmed.

Its paste began, but the recipient's CLI did not take the message before the deadline. A
paste its terminal had not taken whole by then still goes in, and no Enter follows it.
The recipient's CLI has no rule to read its input by, so Facade Code Framework types no message into it.

DeliveryFailure.description: Why a message was not delivered.

oneOf.description: The message is being delivered, or waits for its guest's next turn.
The message was delivered.
The message was not delivered.

DeliveryStatus.description: The state of a message's delivery.

oneOf.description:
Neither service held the CLI's terminal, so it closed. A CLI that ignores hangup may still
be running.

EndReason.description: Why an exit has no code or signal.

above.description: Rows hidden above the visible input, or 1 where the CLI marks hidden rows without counting them.

below.description: Rows hidden below the visible input, or 1 where the CLI marks hidden rows without counting them.

HiddenRows.description: Rows of a draft scrolled out of the CLI's input, as the CLI marks them.

oneOf.description: It exited with code 0.
Facade Code Framework stopped it.
It exited with another code, or a signal ended it.

evidence.description:
What on the screen the state rests on, such as `the input frame at row 22 is empty`. Never
the draft's text.

mechanism.description: The layout the agent's CLI rule reads. Omitted without a rule.

hidden.description: Draft rows scrolled out of the input. Omitted unless the CLI marks such rows.

InputInfo.description: An agent's message input as its screen shows it now.

oneOf.description: A prompt row inside a frame of two rules.
A prompt row above a model line at the bottom of the screen.
An editor between two rules, with a cursor the CLI draws.
A box of bar rows above a border.
The last row that starts with the prompt.

InputMechanism.description: The layout a CLI's rule reads its input from.

oneOf.description: The CLI's input is drawn empty.
The CLI's input holds text, typed, pasted, or recalled.
A menu or question of the CLI's own is drawn in place of its input.
The screen does not show the input as the CLI's rule describes it.

InputState.description: How an agent's message input reads on its screen. A reading never means input may be typed.

location_id.description:
`loc-` followed by 16 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the location's path: the same in
every window that lists it.

label.description: The checkout's branch, or else the folder's name.

path.description: The absolute path, with symbolic links resolved.

kind.description: What the location is: a folder, a repository's main checkout, or a linked worktree.

source_folder.description: The requested workspace folder that produced this local result.

oneOf.description: A folder outside any Git checkout, or one inside a checkout that is not its root.
A repository's main checkout.
A linked worktree of a repository.

Overrides.description: Whether a start can choose a CLI's model and its effort.

code.description:
The exit code, if the CLI exited normally and its status is known. On Windows every exit
has one: the process's 32-bit exit code carried as an `i32`, so that 0xC000013A is
-1073741510.

signal.description:
The terminating signal name, such as `SIGKILL`. Signal numbers vary by system. Never on
Windows.

reason.description:
Why no code or signal is available, if known. If all three fields are absent, the exit
status is unavailable.

at.description:
The exit time in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds. For an exit without a code or
signal, the time Facade Code Framework noticed it.

ProcessExit.description:
A recorded CLI exit. Without a code or signal, its status is unavailable; do not treat it as
exit code zero.

PromptOutcome.description: A start prompt's message ID and what became of it.

text.description: The text on one line, at most 1,024 characters.

from.description: Who said it: an agent ID, or `human` for the person.

from_name.description: The agent's name when it said it. Omitted for the person.

at.description: When, in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds.

Said.description:
The latest submission through an agent's terminal, from a person, an `agent.type` call with
`enter`, or a message Facade Code Framework delivered.

oneOf.description: The normal screen, with scrollback.
The alternate screen, which a full-screen view draws on. It has no scrollback.

ScreenBuffer.description: The screen buffer a CLI shows.

SshInteraction.description: A diagnostic and the command that repairs the saved SSH connection.

SshTransport.description: Normalized SSH arguments, including an empty argv when no options are required.

kind.description: What the CLI waits for, on `waiting_for_you`.

text.description:
The CLI's own words where it gave any, on `waiting_for_you` and on an `error` the CLI
reported. Untrusted text on one line.

how.description:
How the process ended, on `ended`. Omitted when its exit status is unavailable and Facade Code Framework
did not stop it; `exit.reason` says what is known.

reason.description:
Why nothing shows what the CLI is doing, on `unknown`, or what Facade Code Framework found wrong, on an
`error` it found: a start that showed nothing, or tools the CLI cannot use.

oneOf.description: `unknown`: a program without a rule has shown nothing of what it is doing since it started.
`unknown`: the CLI asked to report what it is doing and has not reported since.

`unknown`: the CLI took back what it reported, or a full reset or a shell's new prompt ended
it.
`unknown`: the CLI's screen shows nothing its rule recognizes.

`error`: a CLI started by its rule's name showed nothing of what it is doing within 30
seconds of its start or resume.
`error`: the CLI cannot use the Facade Code Framework tools it was given; `tools_reason` says why.

StateReason.description: Why nothing shows what an agent's CLI is doing, or what Facade Code Framework found wrong with it.

oneOf.description: None of it.
Part of it.
All of it.

Not known: the recipient read the message while its typist was typing it, its typist did not
say by the deadline, what it typed was still queued then, to reach the terminal once the CLI
reads, or the daemon before a restart had begun its paste.

TextWritten.description: How much of a message reached the recipient's terminal.

oneOf.description: Facade Code Framework could not give them to this run's CLI; the daemon's log says why.

Its Facade Code Framework server did not connect within 30 seconds of the run's start or resume, or of a
daemon's recovery of the run.

Its CLI starts its servers only with its first turn or its panel of servers, and the run's
start could not have the panel start Facade Code Framework's server before the first turn; the daemon's log
says why. The first turn starts it.
Its Facade Code Framework server's last connection closed while the run went on.
The CLI ended.

ToolsReason.description: Why an agent's CLI cannot use the Facade Code Framework tools it was given.

oneOf.description: The CLI was not given the tools: it has no rule, or its rule does not give them.
The CLI was given the tools, and its server has not answered the CLI's `tools/list` yet.
The CLI's server answered its `tools/list` and holds a connection.
The CLI was given the tools but cannot use them; `tools_reason` says why.

ToolsState.description:
Whether an agent's CLI can use Facade Code Framework's tools: `facade-mcp`, the MCP server that a CLI started
by its rule is given for its run.

oneOf.description: The person's permission to go on.
The person's answer to a question.
The person to sign in.
The CLI did not say.
